sections.h2: Which selling routes does a Miami homeowner have?
sections.html:
Three routes exist: hire an agent, handle it yourself, or accept cash from an investor who buys without repairs. Each one gives up something, either price, speed or effort, and the best fit hinges on your loan balance, the state of the house and your deadline.

Within Miami's 36.00 square miles of land live an estimated 489,812 people as of July 2025, which is 10.8 percent more than the 2020 base. The 2020 census density was 12,285.8 per square mile. Housing types vary block to block, so a neighbor's sale is a weak guide to your own price.

  • Agent: the most exposure, plus showings, repair requests and a longer wait.
  • Do it yourself: you price, advertise, negotiate and handle the paperwork.
  • Investor cash: few showings and a quicker close, normally below what a fixed-up listing earns.
  • Keep and rent: only if the zoning and city rules in the next sections allow your plan.

sections.h2: How common is home ownership in Miami?
sections.html:
Renters dominate here. Owners occupy just 30.8 percent of the 194,821 households counted from 2020 through 2024, with 2.32 people in a typical household.

The same Census page records 57.7 percent of residents as foreign-born and 77.2 percent of those five and older using another language at home. Plan for bilingual showings and for a contract the signers fully understand.

sections.h2: Could I rent my Miami house short term rather than sell?
sections.html:
Seldom. The city holds that houses and duplexes in the T3 and T4-R transect zones are generally ineligible for short-term rental or lodging use, a position it ties to City of Miami v. Airbnb.

Apartment and condo conversions face a longer list: a Certificate of Occupancy, a state lodging license from the Department of Business and Professional Regulation, a Certificate of Use, a Business Tax Receipt and any county approvals. The Certificate of Use then renews every year, and the city may audit or inspect without notice.

Once more than 25 percent of a building's units are used as short-term rentals, the city treats the building as transient, which triggers a change of occupancy classification and extra building code work. Confirm zoning with the city's zoning department before counting on rental income.

sections.h2: What does a Miami closing cost in taxes and fees?
sections.html:
Miami-Dade stands apart on deed stamps. The state revenue department lists 60 cents per $100 plus a 45 cent surtax, and no surtax when the document moves only a single-family dwelling; the other counties use 70 cents.

A mortgage on the property counts toward the price, so paying it off does not shrink the base. Everyone who signs is liable, which makes the payment clause in the contract worth reading closely.

  • Clerk recording, set by section 28.24 of the Florida Statutes.
  • Payoffs for mortgages, judgments and unpaid taxes.
  • A settlement statement from the title company, which you should see before signing.

sections.h2: How do Miami-Dade taxes work when a Miami house sells?
sections.html:
Property tax runs through two county offices, with the appraiser assessing and the tax collector billing. The appraiser says it neither mails bills nor sets or collects taxes, so call the collector about what you owe.

Its public notice says the appraiser certified the 2026 tax roll on October 16, 2026, and that the June 1 estimate of countywide taxable value was $540.7 billion, up 5.5 percent from 2025. To contest a value, a petition must reach the clerk inside a 25-day window that starts with the proposed tax notice, and it is heard by the value adjustment board.

After a homestead sells, the next owner is assessed at full value starting the next January 1. If you are buying again in Florida, ask the appraiser about portability, which is requested together with the new homestead application by March 1.

sections.h2: How do I handle liens, repairs or code problems in Miami?
sections.html:
A cash sale can still close, but each item has to be cleared or priced. A title search turns up mortgages, judgments and unpaid taxes, and a bill unpaid after April 1 becomes delinquent with certificates sold by June 1.

Open permits and unpermitted work often surface in older buildings. Ask the city's building department what is open on your parcel, and ask the buyer whether the offer takes the work as is.

  • Inherited house: the estate may need court authority before anyone can sign a deed.
  • Past-due mortgage: get the payoff and case status from the lender in writing.
  • Tenant in place: Florida sets a 3-day written demand for unpaid rent, not counting weekends or court holidays, and a 30-day notice to end a monthly tenancy.

sections.h2: What happens once the Miami deed is signed?
sections.html:
At closing the clerk of court records the deed and takes the stamp tax while the title company clears liens. The state names warranty, special warranty, quit claim and trustee's deeds among taxable deeds, so switching the form does not dodge the tax.

The appraiser's site also promotes a no-cost clerk alert that pings you within a day when a deed or mortgage is filed under your name. Enroll before and after a sale to see what was filed.

Tell the appraiser's office when a homestead property sells, and keep the settlement statement with your tax records.

sections.h2: What help does the Miami-Dade appraiser offer owners?
sections.html:
The appraiser's office runs two public branches, one downtown and one in Cutler Bay, and it schedules appointments online. It also holds neighborhood outreach events where staff review values, exemptions and portability one on one.

Widow and widower exemptions, and disability exemptions for veterans or their surviving spouses, can now be filed online, with document uploads. Agricultural classification applications are online too.

If you suspect homestead exemption fraud on a neighboring property, the appraiser's compliance department takes reports. For a sale, the most useful step is to look up your parcel's exemptions and assessed value online, and bring that printout to any pricing conversation.

sections.h2: How do I size up a Miami cash offer?
sections.html:
Set it against the proceeds of a listing once fees, fix-ups and months of upkeep are subtracted. In the contract, find who pays the deed stamp, the title policy and recording, and what becomes of the deposit.

Ask for the settlement date and the closing agent in writing. Hold off signing the deed until the contract is final, and pay no fee merely to receive an offer. If you cannot decide, request a second offer from a different buyer and compare the terms line by line.

faqs.q: Is Miami's deed tax higher than elsewhere in Florida?
faqs.a: Miami-Dade uses 60 cents plus a 45 cent surtax per hundred dollars, and a deed for only a single-family home owes no surtax. Other counties use 70 cents.

faqs.q: Can a Miami single-family house be a short-term rental?
faqs.a: Generally no. The city says single-family and duplex structures in T3 and T4-R transect zones are generally ineligible. Ask the zoning department about your parcel.

faqs.q: Who sends my Miami property tax bill?
faqs.a: The Miami-Dade tax collector does. The property appraiser values the property and states plainly that it mails no bills.

faqs.q: May heirs sell a Miami house they inherited?
faqs.a: Yes, after someone has court authority to sign. Summary administration covers non-exempt estates up to $150,000 or a death that occurred over two years ago.

faqs.q: Is my reduced assessment passed to the next owner?
faqs.a: No. The buyer starts at full assessed value after the next January 1, although you could move your saved amount to your next Florida homestead.
